title: Send for Krishna
hookLine: everyone in the hall says yes, and Yudhishthira still sends for Krishna, the friend who sees further
carry: krishna, the friend who sees further
last: WHAT WE DO STILL REACHES THE ANCESTORS.

cards: Narada has one more thing to say before he goes. This sacrifice, he tells the king, is hard to finish. It has many obstacles.
Brahma-rakshasas, demons who haunt sacrifices, look for any flaw in it. And after it, a war can come that destroys the warriors of the earth. Think it over, Narada says.
Do what's good for you. Then he leaves, and the hall is left holding both halves of the message.

teach.b: A dead father asking his son to rise to this. A sage warning that it might end in ruin. Yudhishthira brushes aside neither.
The text says he sighed, and thought, and couldn't find peace. So he asks. First his ministers and his brothers: you deserve this, they say, do it.
Then the priests and sages, Dhaumya, and Vyasa himself. They agree too.
Everyone in the room says yes. And still Yudhishthira doesn't move. People who love you, he reasons, don't always point out the danger.
So he thinks of the one who won't flatter him and sees further than anyone: Krishna. He sends a fast messenger to Dwaraka, and Krishna comes quickly. Here's why that matters to Hindus.
Krishna isn't just a clever cousin.
Many Hindus worship him as God himself, Vishnu come into the world, and the Mahabharata keeps showing him in one role above all: the friend at your side who sees what you can't.
Devotees even have a name for loving God this way: sakhya, friendship, one of the moods of bhakti. Watch for it.
Later in this serial, on a battlefield, Arjuna will turn to the same friend in his worst hour, and what Krishna says there becomes the Bhagavad Gita.

Today is the small first version: a good king, surrounded by yeses, who still wants Krishna's eyes on it. Many Hindus still bring a big choice to God first, at the home shrine or the temple, before they decide.

how: Many Hindus keep a picture or murti of Krishna at the home shrine and bring big decisions there first; devotees speak of loving him as a friend, sakhya, one of the moods of bhakti.

o: a vow a king makes before a great sacrifice
demons that hunt for flaws in a sacred rite
a hall, and the counsel of those who gather there

games.q: the warning and the counsel — tap the pairs.
p: warns the sacrifice is hard to finish

s: Narada promised the Rajasuya would go smoothly
he warned it has many obstacles and that a war can come after it.
many Hindus worship Krishna as God and love him as a friend
Vishnu come into the world; devotees call that love sakhya, friendship.
Yudhishthira acted as soon as everyone agreed
he still sent for Krishna, wanting someone who wouldn't just please him.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira. your ministers, your brothers and the sages all say perform the Rajasuya. what do you do?
o: send for Krishna and ask him.
drop the idea because of Narada's warning.
games.why: he sends a fast messenger to Dwaraka. he wants Krishna's sight, not one more vote. later, Arjuna turns to the same friend on a battlefield, and Krishna's answer becomes the Gita.

practice: Think of a choice in front of you. If you have a home shrine or a picture of Krishna, sit in front of it; if not, just close your eyes.
Say the choice plainly, out loud or inside, the way Yudhishthira laid it out for Krishna, and then stop talking and listen for a minute. If you pray, ask to see it the way Krishna would.
If you don't, ask what the wisest person you know would see that you're missing.

wordCard.voice: Sabha. A hall full of counsel. Today, every voice in it says yes, and the king still sends for Krishna.

orig.note: Sanskrit nārada: the wandering sage who brings Pandu's request and the warning, then leaves.

carryVoice: Your line: krishna, the friend who sees further. Everyone said yes, and the king still asked him. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Lokapala Sabhakhyana Parva (Narada's warning) and Rajasuyarambha Parva (Yudhishthira consults ministers, brothers, Dhaumya and Vyasa, and sends for Krishna)
